newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes low in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes low in thin trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed low on Monday, in thin trade which was volatile due to late commercial demand, speculation and high call money rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.60 to the dollar, after opening at 58.48, they said.
"The dollar-rupee exchange rate was volatile because movements were greatly exaggerated due to the market being thin," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
The forex market, which was lethargic early, picked up towards mid-day due to some import covering, speculation and banks generating rupees, he said.
Overnight call money rates closed at 12 percent, after opening at 16, dealers said.
"Money was volatile because banks were covering positions ahead of the mid-week holiday," said one.
Wednesday and Thursday are holidays due to a religious festival.
